transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Gallagher (CTO, Argentum), Maya Ortiz (CISO, Argentum), Ben Lowe (Product Manager, Argentum)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on data residency and compliance needs for Argentum Bank evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private Redwood deployments. Main concerns: EU data residency, audit log granularity and retention, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML and RBAC, PCI scope reduction and potential HIPAA mention for a small health-fintech line. Agreed next steps include sending security pack and scheduling a private-deploy deep dive + PoC on Dedicated.

Topics:
- Current stack and where LLM inference would be integrated
- Data residency: EU/UK vs US storage and processing
- Logging restrictions: PII redaction, minimal logs, retention windows
- Compliance: SOC2, ISO, PCI, GDPR; brief HIPAA question from product team (edge case)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and costs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros, um I'm Alex with Redwood, I'm the AE on this.
[00:08] Tom Gallagher: Tom here, CTO at Argentum. We've got Maya our CISO and Ben on product.
[00:13] Maya Ortiz: Hi, thanks.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood infra, hi all.
[00:18] Ben Lowe: Hey.
[00:20] Alex Reed: Cool. Quick agenda, we'll clarify your compliance and residency requirements then go into deployment options and follow with next steps.
[00:28] Tom Gallagher: Sounds good. To start, our main driver is we want to add summary and routing features over customer messages, but we need to make sure customer data stays in-region, mostly EU for our retail division and US for wealth. So residency is big.
[00:41] Priya Nair: Got it. Do you have strict processing-in-region requirements or is storage-only?
[00:47] Tom Gallagher: Processing in-region. EU data must not leave eu-west-1 for processing. Logs we prefer to keep minimal, and retention is 90 days for logs, 7 years for audit artifacts in some cases.
[00:58] Maya Ortiz: Also want very strict audit logs, but we want to avoid token-level logging of PII; ideally redaction or pseudonymization before any logs are stored.
[01:09] Alex Reed: Understood. So high-level, Redwood offers Hosted (multi-tenant but regionally segmented), Dedicated (reserved pools in a region/account), and Private (VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking and control plane). Each has different control levels for residency and logging.
[01:26] Ben Lowe: Can Hosted meet our EU processing requirement?
[01:29] Priya Nair: Hosted can support EU-only processing for many customers, but guaranteed controls depend on contractual commitments and the hosting region— there's still a shared infra layer. For bank-level controls you'd likely look at Dedicated or Private. Hosted is quickest to go live.
[01:42] Tom Gallagher: Ok, so Dedicated would give us reserved GPU pools in eu-west-1 and we could configure retention?
[01:49] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated gives you tenant isolation and more configurability: log sinks, retention policies, and you can opt to disable token-level logging. We can also integrate with your KMS so keys are customer managed — important for PCI/crypto controls.
[02:03] Maya Ortiz: About KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys or bring-your-own-key?
[02:08] Priya Nair: We support KMS integrations — bring your own key (BYOK) via standard key wrapping and in, um, some cases HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. Hosted supports BYOK with cloud KMS. For Private, if you want HSM on-prem we can support that in the Private bundle.
[02:22] Tom Gallagher: What about audit logs? We need full request/response hash-level audit for compliance but without storing raw PII. How do you handle that?
[02:31] Alex Reed: Typical pattern is to enable structured audit logs with redaction hooks. Redwood can redact or hash sensitive fields before logs are persisted; we also support configurable retention and external log sinks (SIEM, Splunk, S3). Note: for Hosted we need to ensure contractual logs don't cross region boundaries.
[02:47] Maya Ortiz: And is that redaction done client-side or server-side? We prefer client-side before hitting the net.
[02:53] Priya Nair: You can do pre-ingest redaction client-side and also configure server-side policies. For tighter controls you'd do both— client-side to limit exposure and server-side as a safety net.
[03:04] Ben Lowe: For GDPR, do you have support for data subject requests and deletion? If a user asks to be forgotten, how does Redwood make that easy?
[03:12] Alex Reed: We have deletion tooling and APIs; for Dedicated and Private you have direct access to storage so you can run deletions in-region. Hosted has a deletion workflow with contractual SLAs — we can map the data lifecycle in the security pack we'll send.
[03:26] Tom Gallagher: Ok. One of our engineering constraints is we run on Kubernetes and prefer service endpoints inside our VPC. Would Private allow us to host the inference nodes in our VPC?
[03:36] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. That gives you total network control, private subnets, and peered connectivity. It does add deployment complexity and typically a longer lead time and enterprise licensing.
[03:48] Maya Ortiz: Risk question — do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation? And PCI? We need PCI scoping guidance if we're touching cardholder data.
[03:56] Alex Reed: We maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO/27001 reports; PCI is handled on a per-customer basis — for many banks we recommend tokenization or offloading card data so the inference endpoint never sees raw PANs which reduces PCI scope. We'll include relevant attestation copies in the security pack.
[04:12] Tom Gallagher: Good. Another practical point: logging retention. For some regs we must retain audit artifacts for 7 years. Can Redwood export immutable archives to our S3 in eu-west-1?
[04:23] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated and Private support export to customer S3 buckets and retention policies. We can set up write-once rules on your bucket side. Hosted can forward to your S3 via cross-account but we'd want to confirm region residency.
[04:36] Ben Lowe: Do you have examples of other banks using Redwood Private?
[04:40] Alex Reed: We do; I'll share anonymized architecture references and a case study.
[04:44] Maya Ortiz: We also need SSO and RBAC for admin and developer access. SAML? SCIM?
[04:50] Priya Nair: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. Role-based access controls with least-privilege roles are standard; for Private you can hook into your IdP directly.
[04:59] Tom Gallagher: On costs — Dedicated vs Private — rough delta?
[05:03] Alex Reed: Dedicated is reserved capacity in our managed fleet — predictable hourly costs and lower ops overhead. Private includes licensing and often a larger uplift due to network and deployment support, but gives the most control. We'll send a pricing matrix.
[05:15] Ben Lowe: Any thoughts on latency for Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted? We need sub-200ms 95th percentile for short prompts in wealth product.
[05:24] Priya Nair: Latency mostly depends on placement and instance type; Private in VPC close to your apps can be lowest, Dedicated in the same region is comparable. We'll run benchmarks during PoC to ensure 95th pct meets your SLO.
[05:37] Tom Gallagher: We also have strict logging restrictions — legal team insists on no verbatim storage of user-generated content in logs. How does Redwood ensure accidental capture is avoided?
[05:48] Alex Reed: We can disable request/response logging entirely and keep only metadata, or we can store hashed fingerprints. There is usually a compromise: keep sufficient audit for replay/hash verification while avoiding raw content. We'll include configuration examples.
[06:03] Maya Ortiz: We saw mention of KV cache; caching is great for cost but could be a risk if PII is cached. How does that work?
[06:10] Priya Nair: KV cache can be configured to skip sensitive prefixes and to evict quickly; for banks you'd use cache policies that exclude PII or use client-side redaction before the model sees it.
[06:20] Ben Lowe: On encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS? Customer-managed keys?
[06:24] Alex Reed: TLS for transit; at-rest encryption via platform-managed keys or customer-managed via KMS. Private supports HSM-backed options.
[06:32] Tom Gallagher: HIPAA — we have a small healthcare vertical, is Redwood HIPAA-capable?
[06:36] Priya Nair: We have customers in regulated spaces; HIPAA coverage is possible but requires BAAs and specific deployment patterns (usually Dedicated or Private). We'll note that in the security pack.
[06:47] Maya Ortiz: One more technical thing — where are model artifacts stored? If we bring our own models, can they be stored in our region?
[06:54] Priya Nair: For Dedicated you can pin model versions and we can host them in-region; for Private you can host artifacts entirely on your infrastructure. Hosted uses our catalog but we do offer bring-your-own-model (BYOM) options with limitations around storage location.
[07:07] Tom Gallagher: Timeline: we want a PoC in the next 3-4 weeks and then a Q2 pilot if all good. Is that reasonable?
[07:15] Alex Reed: That's reasonable. We'll scope a 2-week PoC focused on residency, redaction, and latency benchmarks. Priya will handle the tech setup.
[07:22] Ben Lowe: On the PoC size, can we test with redacted real traffic? We can scrub data but keep shapes.
[07:28] Priya Nair: Yes, scrubbed real traffic is ideal — ensures realistic token lengths and usage patterns.
[07:31] Tom Gallagher: Anything else from Redwood?
[07:34] Alex Reed: We'll send a security and compliance pack, pricing + deployment options, and propose dates for the deep technical dive.
[07:41] Maya Ortiz: We'll share our internal compliance matrix and final decision stakeholders.
[07:45] Alex Reed: Great — recap: security pack + SOC2/ISO + PCI guidance, schedule deep dive, provision PoC on Dedicated in eu-west-1, customer to share compliance matrix.
[07:56] Ben Lowe: Sounds good.
[07:58] Tom Gallagher: Thanks everyone.
[08:00] Alex Reed: Thanks, talk soon.

End notes: Slight transcription errors present (company/product names sometimes hyphenated or missing), but key compliance items captured.
